original.target_description: Problem 11: comparative risk choice (Plan N) under do-your-best versus specific $250,000 savings goal. The two displayed parts are experimental conditions of one between-groups test.

n.location: Printed p. 94 (PDF p. 16), Problem 11 response rows
n.quote:
Which plan will you choose? [Do your best, N ⫽ 65]           Plan N (24%)
        Which plan will you choose? [Save $250,000, N ⫽ 66] Plan N (47%)
n.sample_role: Participants responding to the specified scenario/question.
n.exclusions: No exclusions reported for this problem.

p.quote:
The number of people who choose the more risky Plan N doubles when
people have a specific rather than a ‘‘do your best’’ goal (p ⬍ .01 by χ 2 ).

notes: Published 1999 Cognitive Psychology article, Goals as Reference Points, by Chip Heath, Richard P. Larrick and George Wu. Unassigned replication is a placeholder. n lists the two printed condition sample sizes (65 do-your-best; 66 specific goal), without deriving a combined N. The printed p value is for their comparison, not a separate within-condition test. No numerical chi-square statistic is printed.
